climate.overview_html: The WMO’s September–October–November 2026 Seasonal Outlook forecasts the El Niño Niño 3.4 anomaly peaking near 3.6°C in November–December — now projected as the strongest El Niño in the modern instrumental record, with above-normal temperatures forecast across virtually all land areas through at least early 2027. Pacific island leaders gathered for the Pre-COP in Fiji and Tuvalu (5–8 October) to set the agenda for COP31 in Antalya, Turkey (November), urging delegates to keep 1.5°C alive, integrate the ocean-climate nexus, and close the $310–$365 billion annual adaptation finance gap. The US Supreme Court heard oral arguments on 5 October in Boulder, Colorado’s climate liability lawsuit against ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy — a ruling that will determine whether dozens of similar state and local government suits can proceed in state courts.

items.headline: WMO Seasonal Outlook SON 2026: El Niño Niño 3.4 Forecast to Peak ~3.6°C in November–December — Strongest in Modern Instrumental Record; Above-Normal Temperatures Across Virtually All Land Areas Through Early 2027
items.summary: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update for September–October–November 2026 forecasts the Niño 3.4 SST anomaly reaching approximately 3.6°C during the SON 2026 season, with the intensification trajectory peaking in November–December — a level that would make the 2026 El Niño the strongest in the modern instrumental record, surpassing the 1997–98 event. Above-normal temperatures are forecast with increased likelihood across virtually all land areas through at least early 2027. A concurrent positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD ≈ +0.6°C) and warm tropical Atlantic reinforce the global warming signal. The Super El Niño's fingerprints — drought in Southeast Asia and the western US, flooding risk along eastern Pacific coastlines, and amplified shear suppressing the Atlantic hurricane season — will persist well into 2027.

items.headline: Pre-COP Fiji and Tuvalu (5–8 October): Pacific Leaders Press for 1.5°C Commitment, Ocean-Climate Nexus Integration in COP31 Agenda; $310–365 Billion Annual Adaptation Finance Gap; 50+ Countries Represented
items.summary: More than 50 countries gathered in Nadi, Fiji for the Pacific Pre-COP (5–8 October 2026), co-hosted by Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia, to set the agenda for COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye in November. Forum included on-site visits to Tuvalu to document sea-level rise affecting permanent residents. Fiji's climate minister outlined three priorities: keeping 1.5°C within reach, ensuring climate finance reaches vulnerable communities, and giving the ocean its rightful place in the international climate regime. A UN report released in August found developing countries need $310–$365 billion annually for adaptation while receiving only $26 billion in 2023. A draft COP31 presidency text on ocean protections circulated at Pre-COP — the first time ocean warming and acidification are proposed as a standalone agenda item at a UNFCCC conference.

items.source: Washington Post / NBC News / Claims Journal
items.headline: US Supreme Court Hears Boulder, Colorado Climate Liability Case Against ExxonMobil and Suncor; Ruling Could Determine Fate of Dozens of State and Local Government Climate Lawsuits; Justices Appear ‘Stumped’
items.summary: The US Supreme Court heard oral arguments on October 5, 2026 in a case where Boulder, Colorado seeks to hold ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy liable for climate change damages and for allegedly misleading the public about fossil fuels' climate risks. Boulder officials argue they face mounting wildfire and flood costs. The oil companies seek to remove the case to federal court, where fossil-fuel liability claims face a higher dismissal bar, arguing that allowing state-court climate suits would give states sweeping power over conduct far outside their borders. The case's outcome will determine whether dozens of similar lawsuits by states, cities and counties — involving San Francisco, New York City, Hawaii and others — can proceed in state courts. NBC News reported the justices appeared 'stumped' by the procedural complexities.

items.headline: Super El Niño Kelvin Waves Now Raising US West Coast Sea Levels 15–30 cm; Erosion and Flooding Risk From California to Alaska Through February; Waves Moving North at 150 Miles Per Day
items.summary: A series of oceanic Kelvin waves tied to the 2026 Super El Niño began striking the US Pacific coast in early October, raising sea levels 15–30 cm along the California shoreline and moving north at approximately 150 miles per day toward Oregon and Washington. The surge is expected to continue through February. Experts warn it combines with above-average North Pacific swell and larger-than-average spring tides from October to February — creating compounded erosion and coastal flooding risk for shorelines already experiencing chronic retreat. The wave was expected to reach Alaska by mid-October.

items.headline: Swiss Glaciers Lose 5.5% of Ice Volume in 2026 — Second-Worst Annual Melt on Record; Aletsch Sets Record Since 1870; Alpine Melt Rate “More Than Twice as High” as Any Prior Five-Year Period; 20% Volume Lost Since 2021
items.summary: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their total ice volume in 2026, the second-largest annual ice loss in the instrumental record after 5.9% in 2022. GLAMOS reported that the record-breaking European heatwave of summer 2026 combined with an unusually snow-poor winter to accelerate melting across the Alps. The Aletsch Glacier recorded its biggest annual melt since systematic monitoring began in 1870. Over the past five years (2021–2026), Switzerland has lost nearly 20% of its total glacier ice volume — a rate 'more than twice as high as in any previously monitored five-year period.'

items.headline: Copernicus Ocean State Report 10 (OSR10): Mediterranean Hits Two-Decade High in Marine Heatwave Days; Arctic Ice Declining 490,000 km²/Decade; Black Sea and Mediterranean +4.6°C Peak Marine Heatwave Intensity; Ocean Heat Content Record in 2025
items.summary: The Copernicus Marine Service released its 10th Ocean State Report (OSR10) on September 30, 2026. Key findings: the Mediterranean Sea recorded its highest number of marine heatwave days in the 20-year record; the Black Sea and Mediterranean experienced peak marine heatwave intensity more than 4.6°C above normal in 2024; Arctic sea ice is declining at nearly 490,000 km² per decade; Mediterranean SSTs rose at 0.32°C per decade from 1982–2024; and global ocean heat content reached its highest level on record in 2025.

items.headline: EU Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework Due October 20: 3°C Reference Scenario; Duty on ‘Risk Owners’ Across Key Sectors; 100 Vulnerable Territories Identified
items.summary: The European Commission is due to present its Integrated Climate Resilience and Risk Management Framework on October 20, 2026 — a legislative package embedding 'climate resilience by design' across EU policy. The framework establishes a 3°C global warming reference scenario as the mandatory planning baseline; a legal duty to assign 'risk owners' for every major climate risk in key sectors (agriculture, transport, energy, finance, health); identification of 100 vulnerable European territories; and measures to mobilize private investment for resilience.

major_events.name: Typhoon Choi-Wan (JTWC 27W) — WEAKENING; EXTRATROPICAL TRANSITION UNDERWAY; CLEAR OF OGASAWARA
major_events.status: ACTIVE — As of 6 October, Choi-Wan has weakened to 125 mph / 200 km/h from its peak of 241 km/h / 912 hPa; now located at 27.3°N, 145.9°E moving NNW at 5 mph; Ogasawara Islands now in the clear; extratropical transition expected as the storm recurves northeast into higher latitudes
major_events.impact: Decreasing but still significant seas (5–8 m) along the storm’s track; JMA maintaining Typhoon Advisory; dangerous swells continuing across southern Philippine Sea and north-central Pacific

major_events.name: Typhoon Nolo (formerly Hurricane Nolo) — TYPHOON; WESTERN PACIFIC; NO IMMEDIATE LAND THREAT
major_events.status: ACTIVE — Hurricane Nolo crossed the International Date Line on October 4 and was reclassified as Typhoon Nolo; now located at 25.7°N, 173.0°E with maximum sustained winds of 105 kt (195 km/h); moving westward at 17 mph; JTWC forecasts gradual weakening to tropical storm status by October 7; general track toward Japan but no watches or warnings issued; only the second dateline-crossing storm since Hurricane Dora (2023)
major_events.impact: Hazardous seas across central North Pacific; no current coastal warnings or watches for populated areas

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Koguma (JTWC 28W) — NEWLY FORMED; MARSHALL ISLANDS VICINITY; POTENTIAL SUPER TYPHOON
major_events.status: ACTIVE — Tropical Storm Koguma formed near the Marshall Islands (11°N, 168°E) on October 5 with maximum sustained winds ~40 mph (35 kt); JTWC 5-day forecast projects rapid intensification to 105 kt (121 mph), potentially Super Typhoon status; 7-day track shows recurvature east of Japan; model guidance shows large spread beyond day 5
major_events.impact: Currently no land threat; deep warm water anomalies from the Super El Niño providing exceptional intensification potential; would be the fourth Super Typhoon of the 2026 western Pacific season if JTWC forecast verifies

major_events.name: Atlantic Invest 92L / Potential Tropical Storm Isaias — DEVELOPMENT LIKELY; GULF COAST APPROACH EXPECTED OCTOBER 8–12
major_events.status: ACTIVE — NHC now gives Invest 92L a 60% 2-day / 80% 7-day development probability, upgraded from 40% on October 4; tropical depression formation expected mid-week; if named, would become Tropical Storm Isaias (9th named Atlantic storm of 2026); expected to drift eastward then northward toward the US Gulf Coast by October 8–12
major_events.impact: Heavy rainfall and coastal flooding possible along Gulf Coast and Florida this week regardless of tropical cyclone classification; storm surge risk elevated if Isaias achieves tropical storm intensity near landfall

major_events.name: Hurricane Rachel — EASTERN PACIFIC; WEAKENING; NO LAND THREAT
major_events.status: ACTIVE — Rachel continues weakening in the Eastern Pacific south-southwest of Baja California; dry-air entrainment and wind shear accelerating weakening; 20th named storm of the 2026 Eastern Pacific season; tracking into open Central Pacific
major_events.impact: Diminishing 2–3 m swell along Baja California Pacific coast; no coastal warnings or watches in effect

weather.overview_html: The western Pacific’s ‘typhoon freeway’ is extraordinarily busy: Hurricane Nolo became only the second storm since Dora (2023) to cross the International Date Line and be reclassified as a typhoon on October 4, while newly formed Tropical Storm Koguma (28W) is projected by JTWC to intensify to 105 kt in five days — potentially the fourth Super Typhoon of the 2026 season — as Choi-Wan weakens past Ogasawara and undergoes extratropical transition. In the Atlantic, Invest 92L’s development probability has risen from 40% to 60–80%, with potential Tropical Storm Isaias drifting toward the US Gulf Coast by October 8–12. In Europe, a DANA cold-drop system triggered deadly flash flooding across Eastern Spain on October 2–3, killing one person and prompting 90 rescues in Albacete province after 140 mm fell in under two hours.

items.source: WTOP / Washington Times / The Watchers / Weather.com
items.headline: Hurricane Nolo Crosses International Date Line and Becomes Typhoon Nolo — Only Second Dateline-Crossing Storm Since Hurricane Dora (2023); 105 kt Winds; Westward Track Toward Japan General Direction
items.summary: Hurricane Nolo crossed the International Date Line at approximately 5 p.m. ET on October 4, 2026, entering the western North Pacific and being reclassified by JTWC as Typhoon Nolo — only the second storm to complete this transition since Hurricane Dora in 2023. At the time of crossing, Nolo had maximum sustained winds of 115 mph (185 km/h). The storm is now located near 25.7°N, 173.0°E, moving westward at 17 mph (28 km/h). JTWC forecasts Nolo to gradually weaken but retain typhoon status for approximately three days before downgrading. Forecast models indicate a northwestward turn toward Japan's general direction in coming days, though no watches or warnings have been issued for any populated area.

items.source: Stars and Stripes / Tropical Tidbits / Weather Underground
items.headline: Tropical Storm Koguma (28W) Forms Near Marshall Islands; JTWC Forecasts Rapid Intensification to 105 kt in 5 Days — Potential Fourth Super Typhoon of 2026 Season; Track Points East of Japan
items.summary: Tropical Storm Koguma (JTWC 28W) was designated in the western Pacific near the Marshall Islands on October 5, 2026, with initial maximum sustained winds of approximately 40 mph (35 kt). JTWC's five-day forecast projects rapid intensification to 105 kt (121 mph) — which would make Koguma a Super Typhoon and the fourth of the 2026 western Pacific season. Seven-day track forecasts show Koguma recurving northeastward east of Japan, with large model spread beyond day 5. The deep warm water anomalies associated with the 2026 Super El Niño across the western Pacific are providing an exceptional energy source for rapid intensification, consistent with the unusually high proportion of Super Typhoons this season.

items.headline: NHC Upgrades Atlantic Invest 92L to 60–80% Development Probability; Tropical Depression Expected Mid-Week; Potential Tropical Storm Isaias to Drift Toward US Gulf Coast October 8–12
items.summary: The National Hurricane Center upgraded the development probability of Invest 92L in the southwestern Gulf of America from 40% (October 4) to 60% within two days and 80% over seven days as of October 5, 2026. A tropical depression is now expected to form mid-week. The system is forecast to drift eastward then northward toward the US Gulf Coast, with potential approach by October 8–12. If it achieves tropical storm status, it will be named Isaias — the ninth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic season. The NHC emphasized that heavy rainfall and coastal flooding are likely along the Gulf Coast and in Florida this week regardless of tropical cyclone classification.

items.source: The Watchers / Euronews / World Central Kitchen
items.headline: DANA Cold-Drop Flash Flooding Kills One, Prompts 90 Rescues in Eastern Spain; 140 mm Rain in 2 Hours at Madrigueras, Albacete; Four Homes Collapse; Valencia and Catalonia Also Hit
items.summary: A DANA (Depresión Aislada en Niveles Altos, cut-off low) storm system struck Eastern Spain overnight on October 2–3, 2026, dropping more than 140 mm of rain in approximately two hours at Madrigueras in Albacete Province. The flash flood killed one person (a 102-year-old woman) and prompted rescue of around 90 residents. Four homes collapsed and more than 150 vehicles were submerged or swept away. World Central Kitchen mobilized a response in Madrigueras. The DANA simultaneously affected the Valencia region and Catalonia, and southern France issued red alerts for Hérault and Gard departments. Mediterranean autumn DANA events have intensified in recent years as warmer Mediterranean SSTs provide greater moisture loading.

items.headline: Super Typhoon Choi-Wan Weakens to 125 mph After Passing Ogasawara; Now 27.3°N, 145.9°E Moving NNW; Extratropical Transition Underway; Peak Was 241 km/h / 912 hPa
items.summary: Super Typhoon Choi-Wan has weakened from its peak intensity of 241 km/h (130 kt) / 912 hPa on October 4–5 to approximately 125 mph (~108 kt) as of October 6, now at 27.3°N, 145.9°E moving NNW at 5 mph. The storm has passed the Ogasawara Islands (Chichi-jima and Haha-jima), which experienced their closest approach on October 5–6, and JMA has relaxed some advisories for the island group. Extratropical transition is underway as Choi-Wan tracks into higher latitudes and interacts with the midlatitude westerlies, though the storm continues to generate significant dangerous seas across its expansive wind field.

items.headline: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze: Indonesia’s Worst Wildfire Season in 11 Years; ASEAN Alert Level 3 Active; 12 Million People Under Hazardous Air Quality; Super El Niño Drought Fuels Peat Fires
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Alert Level 3 — the highest tier in its haze warning system — remains active as Indonesia's 2026 wildfire season, its worst in 11 years, sustains transboundary haze across Sumatra, Kalimantan and peninsular Southeast Asia. More than 12 million people face hazardous air quality. School closures continue in parts of Malaysia and Singapore. The Super El Niño is sustaining the crisis through drought conditions across Sumatra and Kalimantan.

renewables.overview_html: Spain’s renewables reached 50.9% of the national power mix in September 2026 per grid operator REE (52.7% including self-consumption), a new monthly record. The week’s main M&A story is India, where KPI Green Energy signed a binding offer on October 5 to acquire 507.9 MW of operating Gujarat wind capacity from Alfanar Group for INR 24.1 billion — the largest operational wind M&A transaction in India this year. Elsewhere, Adani Green’s Khavda BESS continues to hold the world record at 6.63 GWh outside China and McKinsey documents 15–20% higher US solar LCOE than 2023 levels with 120 GW of pipeline stalled by interconnection queue and tariff fragmentation.

items.headline: Spain Renewables Hit 50.9% of Power Mix in September 2026 — New Monthly Record; 52.7% Including Self-Consumption; Wind, Solar and Hydro Drive Record; 50 GW Solar Milestone Passed in February
items.summary: Spain's electricity grid operator Red Electrica de España (REE) confirmed that renewable sources accounted for 50.9% of national electricity generation in September 2026, rising to an estimated 52.7% when distributed self-consumption is included. The result sets a new monthly renewable share record for Spain, driven by strong wind output in northern regions and continued solar capacity additions since Spain crossed the 50 GW solar milestone in February 2026.

items.source: Adani Green Energy / ESS News / PV Magazine India
items.headline: Adani Green Energy Khavda BESS Expands to 6.63 GWh — World’s Largest Single-Location Battery Outside China; Over 50% of India’s Operational BESS at One Site
items.summary: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL) expanded its operational BESS capacity at Khavda, Gujarat from 3.55 GWh to 6.63 GWh on October 2, 2026, commissioning the new block in 10 months from construction start. Khavda now holds the world's largest operational single-location battery installation outside China, accounting for more than 50% of India's total operational BESS capacity of approximately 12.6 GWh.

items.headline: Northland Power Closes CAD$185 Million Financing for 300 MW / 1.2 GWh Poland BESS (Kamionka + Mieczysláwów); 17-Year Capacity Market Contracts; Green Loan Structure
items.summary: Northland Power closed approximately CAD$185 million in project financing on September 30, 2026 for two Polish BESS projects: Kamionka (100 MW / 400 MWh) and Mieczysławów (200 MW / 800 MWh). Both carry 17-year capacity market contracts with the Polish system operator and are structured as green loans supplemented by government grants. Commercial operation is targeted for 2028.

items.headline: U.S. Solar and Storage Face Structural Cost Headwinds: McKinsey Report; Tariff Fragmentation, Land Constraints and 4.5-Year Average Interconnection Queue Raise LCOE 15–20% From 2023; 120 GW Pipeline Stalled
items.summary: A McKinsey & Company report published October 2, 2026 finds trade-policy fragmentation, limited land availability and grid interconnection delays averaging 4.5 years have raised US solar LCOE 15–20% above 2023 levels, stalling an estimated 120 GW of pipeline. The authors recommend accelerated FERC Order 1920 implementation as the highest-priority policy lever to unlock grid capacity.

items.headline: Renalfa IPP and Eurowind Inaugurate 242 MWp Solar + 773 MWh BESS Hybrid Park in Bulgaria; Among Europe’s Largest Operational Hybrid Renewable Parks
items.summary: Romanian IPP Renalfa and Danish developer Eurowind Energy inaugurated a hybrid renewable energy park in Bulgaria combining 242 MWp of solar PV with 773 MWh of battery energy storage — among the largest co-located solar-plus-storage facilities in operational service in Europe. The project reflects growing maturation of hybrid renewable development across Central and Eastern Europe beyond the UK, Germany and Iberia.

items.headline: Australia: Synergy Proposes A$2 Billion Solar and Battery Addition at Warradarge Wind Farm in Western Australia; Would Be Among Largest Hybrid Renewable Projects in Southern Hemisphere
items.summary: Western Australian state-owned utility Synergy unveiled plans to develop a A$2 billion (approximately US$1.3 billion) co-located solar and battery storage project at the recently expanded Warradarge Wind Farm — currently the largest wind farm in the state. The proposal would create one of Australia's largest hybrid renewable energy projects by adding solar PV and grid-scale battery storage to the existing wind infrastructure, leveraging the existing transmission connection and site permits.

science.overview_html: Three new arXiv papers this week push data-driven forecasting frontiers: Varda-single-1.0 (arXiv:2610.01835) presents the first kilometre-scale (1 km) data-driven forecast system trained on regional reanalysis over Alpine topography, matching or outperforming MeteoSwiss’s operational ICON-CH baselines to +120 h; ClimateBench v2.0 (arXiv:2610.04558) establishes a three-tier probabilistic evaluation protocol allowing any physics-based, data-driven or hybrid climate model to be compared on equal footing from energy conservation tests through paleoclimate out-of-distribution challenges; and PTQ of autoregressive weather models (arXiv:2610.02511) demonstrates that 8-bit post-training quantization of DLWP and FourCastNet retains near-full forecast skill, opening a path to edge deployment of global MLWP on drones, balloons and satellites. A new study also shows that warming-driven changes in atmospheric angular momentum are measurably lengthening Earth’s day, with the atmospheric contribution projected to reach 10–18% of tidal friction by 2100.

items.headline: Varda-single-1.0 (arXiv:2610.01835): First Kilometre-Scale Data-Driven Weather Forecast System Over Alpine Topography; Competitive with ICON-CH1-EPS to +33 h, Outperforms ICON-CH2-EPS to +120 h; Dual Graph Transformer Architecture
items.meta: Alberto Pennino et al. · arXiv:2610.01835 (physics.ao-ph, cs.LG) · Submitted 1 October 2026
items.summary: Varda-single-1.0 is the first medium-range data-driven weather prediction system targeting 1 km resolution over the Swiss Alps — notoriously one of the most challenging topographic domains for NWP. The architecture uses two independently trained stretched-grid Graph Transformer encoder–processor–decoder models: a 6-hourly autoregressive global model at 31 km and a temporal downscaler reconstructing hourly 1 km forecasts. The training curriculum follows ERA5 pre-training → 20-year kilometre-scale regional reanalysis fine-tuning → operational km-scale analysis final fine-tuning. Verified over one year, Varda-single is competitive with the 1 km ICON-CH1-EPS control to +33 h and outperforms the 2 km ICON-CH2-EPS control to +120 h. Identified weaknesses: underestimation of local wind maxima and overly smooth convective precipitation. Built on the Anemoi framework, it represents a significant step toward replacing LAM NWP in complex terrain with purely data-driven systems.

items.headline: ClimateBench v2.0 (arXiv:2610.04558): Three-Tier Probabilistic Benchmarking Protocol for Climate Models; Tier I–III from Energy Conservation to Paleoclimate Out-of-Distribution; CRPS Primary Score; All Code and Data Public
items.meta: Duncan Watson-Parris et al. · arXiv:2610.04558 (physics.ao-ph, cs.LG) · Submitted 3 October 2026
items.summary: ClimateBench v2.0 addresses the absence of a standardized multi-tier evaluation protocol that allows physics-based, data-driven and hybrid climate models to be compared on equal terms. Tier I tests physical credibility via energy conservation, coupled co-variability and basic forced responses. Tier II scores models against post-2015 observations of surface temperature, precipitation, radiative fluxes, sea ice and variability modes using fair Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) as the primary metric. Tier III evaluates out-of-distribution generalization through paleoclimate simulations covering the Last Interglacial, Last Glacial Maximum, and Mid-Holocene. All evaluation code, observational data and perfect-model benchmarks are made publicly available, enabling reproducible community-wide comparisons for mid-century regional climate projection skill.

items.headline: Post-Training Quantization of Autoregressive Weather Models (arXiv:2610.02511): 8-Bit PTQ of DLWP and FourCastNet with Minimal Skill Degradation; Path to Edge Deployment of Global MLWP on Drones and Satellites
items.meta: Ananyo Bhattacharya, Swastik Bhattacharya, Christiane Jablonowski · arXiv:2610.02511 (cs.LG, physics.ao-ph) · Submitted 1 October 2026
items.summary: Bhattacharya, Bhattacharya and Jablonowski apply post-training quantization (PTQ) to DLWP (Deep Learning Weather Prediction) and FourCastNet as a proof-of-concept for edge deployment of geophysical deep learning. PTQ compresses a pre-trained model from 32-bit to 8-bit floating-point precision using only a small calibration dataset, with no access to the original training pipeline. Results show 8-bit quantization retains near-full forecast skill for standard atmospheric variables; degradation primarily emerges at 4-bit and below. The practical implication: already-trained production MLWP models could be compressed for deployment on edge hardware — satellites, drones, autonomous balloons — enabling real-time in-situ inference for nowcasting and data assimilation in resource-constrained environments.

items.headline: Climate-Driven Atmospheric Angular Momentum Changes Are Measurably Lengthening Earth’s Day; Atmospheric Contribution Projected to Reach 10–18% of Tidal Friction by 2100; Current Rate Unprecedented in 3.6 Million Years
items.summary: New research published in October 2026 demonstrates that global warming-driven reorganization of atmospheric circulation is measurably influencing Earth's rotational dynamics, increasing atmospheric angular momentum in a way that slightly slows Earth's spin. High-emissions climate simulations project that by 2100, the atmospheric contribution to day-length increase will reach 10–18% of the long-term tidal friction trend. Under a very high emissions scenario, total climate-driven day lengthening could reach 2.62 milliseconds per century — potentially overtaking the Moon's tidal influence on Earth's rotation (approximately 2.4 milliseconds per century). The current measured day-length increase of 1.33 milliseconds per century is itself described as unprecedented in the past 3.6 million years, with both ice-mass redistribution and atmospheric circulation contributing to the signal.

items.source: arXiv / JGR: Machine Learning and Computation
items.headline: AI Emulation of Stochastic Sudden Stratospheric Warmings with Interpretable Latent Structure (arXiv:2610.02069): ResNet CVAE Captures Regime Statistics, Rare Transition Rates and Committor Function of Polar Vortex Disruptions
items.meta: Boscu, Hernandez, Alvarez Ventura, Finkel, Chattopadhyay, Hassanzadeh, Abbot · arXiv:2610.02069 / JGR ML&C doi:10.1029/2026JH001387
items.summary: Boscu et al. develop a probabilistic deep learning emulator for the stochastic Holton-Mass model of stratospheric variability, targeting sudden stratospheric warmings (SSWs) that trigger severe cold outbreaks across Europe and North America. The emulator is a ResNet-inspired Conditional Variational Autoencoder. Key results: accurate reproduction of regime statistics, rare transition rates, the transition committor function, and unsupervised latent PCA separating into four physically interpretable clusters corresponding to strong- vs. weak-vortex and stable- vs. transition-prone configurations — demonstrating that the emulator learns physically meaningful representations, not just matching statistics.

items.headline: Global Heat Stress Intensification (Nature Climate Change Vol. 16): Up to 50 Additional Heat Stress Days Per Year in Most-Impacted Regions; Hottest Nights Warming Faster Than Days (0.32 vs. 0.27°C/Decade); Compound Events Rising Sharply
items.meta: Multiple authors · Nature Climate Change Vol. 16, pp. 989–996 (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02670-5
items.summary: A Nature Climate Change study examining global heat stress found heat stress days increased by up to 50 per year in the most-impacted regions (parts of South Asia, sub-Saharan Africa and the Arabian Peninsula). Tropical nights are warming faster than the hottest days (0.32°C vs. 0.27°C per decade) — a pattern with serious implications for human thermal recovery during heatwaves. Compound daytime–nighttime events increased sharply in frequency since the 2000s. Low- and middle-income countries face disproportionate exposure even as total global heat stress expands.

items.title: KPI Green Energy Signs Binding Offer to Acquire 507.9 MW of Operational Gujarat Wind Capacity from Alfanar Group for INR 24.1 Billion (~US$288M); Largest Operational Wind M&A Deal in India This Year; Close Expected February 2027
items.body_html: KPI Green Energy signed a binding offer on October 5, 2026 to acquire 507.9 MW of operational wind projects in Gujarat from Saudi-backed Alfanar Group for an enterprise value of approximately INR 24.1 billion (US$288 million). The portfolio comprises the Bhuj-1 (301.4 MW, held by Alfanar Energy) and Bhuj-2 (206.5 MW, held by Netra Wind Private Limited) projects in the high-resource Kutch wind corridor. Both projects hold long-term PPAs with the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) with a capacity-weighted remaining life of 21 years, providing strong contracted revenue certainty. The enterprise value translates to approximately INR 48 million per MW — market-consistent for operating Indian wind assets with long-dated SECI offtake. The transaction is expected to close by February 2027, pending regulatory approvals. Following completion, KPI Green’s total operating and under-development portfolio will reach approximately 1.6 GW.

items.title: Euler ILS Partners Signs Multi-Year Catastrophe Risk Analytics Agreement with Moody’s; Access to Natural Catastrophe and Cyber Risk Models, Exposure Datasets and Intelligent Risk Platform; as Cat Bond Issuance Hits Record $65.6 Billion Outstanding
items.body_html: Euler ILS Partners, the specialist Swiss insurance-linked securities investment manager, signed a multi-year agreement on September 29, 2026 with Moody’s to utilise its catastrophe risk models, analytics and exposure datasets via the Moody’s Intelligent Risk Platform™. The agreement grants Euler access to both natural catastrophe and cyber risk models and a range of specialised peril and exposure datasets to inform ILS investment decisions across global markets. The deal follows Moody’s launch of Risk InvestorIQ on September 18, a dedicated catastrophe risk analytics and portfolio management application for ILS professionals. The partnership signals growing institutionalisation of the ILS market, which reached a record $65.6 billion in cat bond issuance outstanding by mid-2026, with H1 2026 new issuance of almost $18 billion also hitting a new high.

items.title: Inox Clean Energy Completes $627.5M Acquisition of Vena Energy India’s 6 GW Renewable Portfolio; Operating Capacity Expands to 4 GW; Total Pipeline Exceeds 12 GW; GIP (BlackRock) Exits India
items.body_html: Indian IPP Inox Clean Energy has completed the acquisition of Vena Energy India for INR 60 billion (US$627.5 million), finalising a deal originally announced in June 2026. The portfolio acquired from BlackRock-owned Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) comprises 1.2 GW of operational assets, 1.8 GW at advanced development stage, and 3 GW of early-pipeline projects across solar, wind and hybrid. Following the transaction, Inox Clean Energy’s operating and near-operational portfolio expands to approximately 4 GW while its total development pipeline exceeds 12 GW, making it one of India’s largest independent renewable energy platforms. The deal marks GIP’s full exit from the Indian renewable energy market and is the largest inbound M&A deal in India’s renewable sector of 2026.
